p0.original: 关键问题：生物医学疗法是怎样治疗心理障碍的
p0.en: Critical question: How biomedical therapy treats mental disorders

p2.original: 生物医学疗法尝试用药物改变大脑的化学反应，通过手术改变大脑的神经通路，或者通过电脉冲或强磁场改变其活动方式来治疗心理障碍。
p2.en: Biomedicine attempts to alter the chemical reaction of the brain with drugs, to alter the neuropaths of the brain through surgery, or to treat psychological disorders by changing the way of activity by electric pulses or powerful magnetic fields.

p3.original: 心理存在于一种微妙的生物平衡中。我们的基因、激素、酶和新陈代谢的不规律性以及事故和疾病造成的损害都可能会扰乱心理状态。当大脑出现问题时，我们可以看到异常行为模式或特殊的认知和情绪反应就会出现。因此，生物医学疗法试图通过直接干预大脑来治疗这些精神障碍。我们的核心概念指定了这些疗法的目标：
p3.en: The mind exists in a delicate biological balance. The irregularity of our genes, hormones, enzymes and metabolisms, as well as the damage caused by accidents and diseases, can disrupt mental health. When the brain is in trouble, we can see an abnormal pattern of behaviour or a special cognitive and emotional reaction. Biomedicine therapy therefore attempts to treat these mental disorders through direct intervention in the brain. Our core concepts define the objectives of these treatments:

p4.original: 生物医学疗法尝试用药物改变大脑的化学反应，通过手术改变大脑的神经通路，或者通过电脉冲或强磁场改变其活动方式来治疗心理障碍。
p4.en: Biomedicine attempts to alter the chemical reaction of the brain with drugs, to alter the neuropaths of the brain through surgery, or to treat psychological disorders by changing the way of activity by electric pulses or powerful magnetic fields.

p5.original: 每一种生物医学疗法都是从精神功能异常的医学模型中产生的，它为精神障碍提供了器质性基础，并将其视为疾病进行治疗。我们从各类精神药物开始研究这些生物医学疗法。
p5.en: Every biomedical therapy is derived from a medical model of abnormal mental function, which provides a physical basis for mental disorders and treats them as diseases. We began to study these biomedical treatments from various psychoactive substances.

p9.en: 13.9 Describe the history of American psychiatric hospitals.

p12.original: 描述药物在治疗精神障碍中的作用。
p12.en: Describe the role of drugs in the treatment of mental disorders.

p13.original: 在有关精神障碍治疗的历史中，没有什么能与发现药物治疗相媲美，这些药物可以使焦虑的患者平静下来，改善抑郁症患者的情绪，并抑制精神病患者的幻觉。这个勇敢的新治疗时代始于1953年，当时第一批抗精神病药物（通常称为“镇静剂”）问世。随着这些药物的广泛应用，许多较难控制、攻击性强的患者几乎奇迹般地变得合作、冷静和可以沟通。此外，许多以前沉迷于妄想和幻觉的思维障碍患者开始对周围的物理和社会环境做出反应。
p13.en: In the history of treatment for mental disorders, there is nothing comparable to the discovery of medications that can calm people with anxiety, improve the mood of people with depression and inhibit the hallucinations of the mentally ill. This brave new era of treatment began in 1953, when the first anti-psychotic drugs, commonly known as “sedigens”, were introduced. With the widespread use of these drugs, many of the more difficult and aggressive patients have become almost miracles of cooperation, calmness and communication. In addition, many people with mental disorders who were previously obsessed with delusions and hallucinations began to react to the physical and social environment surrounding them.

p14.original: 药物治疗的有效性对全美精神病院的普查结果产生了显著影响。1955年，超过50万美国人住在精神病院，每个人的平均住院时间为几年。然后，随着镇静剂的引入，这个数字开始稳步下降。在短短10年多的时间里，实际住在精神病院的人数不到之前的一半，而且通常只住几个月。
p14.en: The effectiveness of drug treatment has had a significant impact on the results of surveys in psychiatric hospitals throughout the United States. In 1955, more than half a million Americans lived in psychiatric hospitals, each for an average period of several years. This figure then began to decline steadily with the introduction of sedatives. In just over 10 years, the actual number of people living in psychiatric institutions is less than half of the previous period and usually only for a few months.

p15.original: 药物治疗早已走出精神病院，走进我们的日常生活中。目前，数以百万计的人因焦虑、压力、抑郁、多动症、失眠、恐惧和恐怖症、痴迷和强迫症、成瘾以及许多其他问题而服用药物。显然，一场药物引发的革命已经到来。
p15.en: The medication has long been removed from the mental institution and has entered our daily lives. At present, millions of people are taking drugs for anxiety, stress, depression, hyperactivity disorder, insomnia, fear and terror, obsession and coercion, addiction and many other problems. Clearly, a drug-induced revolution has arrived.

p16.original: 但这些神奇的药物是什么？
p16.en: But what are these magic drugs?

p17.original: 你可能听说过百忧解和安定，在数十种能改变你的心情、看法、欲望，甚至基本个性的精神药物中，它们只是其中的两种。在这里，我们将考虑当今使用的四大类药物。
p17.en: You may have heard of Prozac and Valium, of which there are only two of the dozens that can change your mood, your perception, your desire, even your basic personality. Here, we will consider the four main types of drugs that are used today.

p19.original: 抗抑郁药物和情绪稳定剂

p23.original: 顾名思义，抗精神病药物（antipsychotics）可以治疗以下精神病症状：妄想、幻觉、社交疏离和情绪激越（Dawkins et al.，1999）。尽管大多数抗精神病药物发挥作用的确切原因尚不清楚，但它们通过降低大脑中神经递质多巴胺的活性来发挥作用。例如，已知氯丙嗪和氟哌啶醇可阻断神经细胞间突触中的多巴胺受体。一种较新的抗精神病药物氯氮平既能降低多巴胺活性，又能增加另一种神经递质血清素的活性，血清素也能抑制多巴胺系统（Javitt & Coyle，2004；Sawa & Snyder，2002）。虽然这些药物会降低大脑的整体活动水平，但它们并不仅仅使患者“平静”下来。相反，它们减少了精神分裂症的“阳性”症状（幻觉、妄想、情绪障碍和激越的行为），尽管它们对许多患者的社交疏离、思维混乱和注意力不集中等“阴性”症状几乎没有作用（Wickelgren，1998a）。近年来，有一些新药上市，但最近的一项研究表明，在减轻精神病症状方面，这些“第二代”抗精神病药物不一定比旧药更有效（Lieberman et al.，2005；Rosenheck et al.，2006）。
p23.en: Anti-psychotics, by definition, treat the following psychiatric symptoms: delusion, hallucinations, social alienation and increased emotional stress (Dawkins et al., 1999). Although the exact reasons for the usefulness of most anti-psychiatric drugs are not yet clear, they work by reducing the activity of neurotransmittance dopamine in the brain. For example, chlorplyazine and fluorine are known to block dopamine receptors in synapses between neurocells. A relatively new antipsychotic drug, chlorazine, can reduce dopamine activity while increasing the activity of another neurotransmitting serum, and serotonin can inhibit the dopamine system (Javitt & Coyle, 2004); Sawa & Snyder, 2002. Although these drugs reduce the overall activity of the brain, they do not simply “settle” the patient. Instead, they reduce the “positive” symptoms of schizophrenia (schizophrenia, delusions, emotional disorders and excesses), although they have little effect on the “negative” symptoms of social alienation, confusion and inoculation of many patients (Wickelgren, 1998a). In recent years, some new medicines have been listed, but a recent study has shown that these “second generation” anti-psychiatry drugs are not necessarily more effective than old ones in reducing psychiatric symptoms (Lieberman et al., 2005); Rosenheck et al., 2006).

p24.original: 不幸的是，长期服用任何抗精神病药物都会产生副作用。已有研究观察到这类药物使得大脑产生一些物理变化（Gur & Maany，1998）。其中最令人担忧的是迟发性运动障碍（tardive dyskinesia），它会导致无法治愈的运动控制障碍，尤其是面部肌肉的控制。虽然一些较新的药物，如氯氮平，由于在阻断多巴胺方面的选择性更强，减少了运动控制方面的副作用，但它们也可能导致严重的问题。
p24.en: Unfortunately, any anti-psychiatric drug that is taken for long periods can have side effects. Studies have been conducted to observe that some physical changes have occurred in the brain (Gur & Maany, 1998). The most worrying of these is the tardive dyskinesia, which can lead to incurable motor control barriers, especially for facial muscles. While newer drugs, such as chlorazine, have reduced side effects in movement control due to greater selectivity in the interdiction of dopamine, they can also lead to serious problems.

p25.original: 冒着风险服用抗精神病药物值得吗？没有简单的答案。我们必须根据患者当前痛苦的严重程度来权衡风险。
p25.en: Is it worth taking antipsychotic drugs at risk? There are no simple answers. We must weigh the risks according to the severity of the suffering that the patient is suffering.

p26.original: 13.7.2 抗抑郁药物和情绪稳定剂

p27.original: 药物治疗还包括使用几种化合物，它们彻底改变了抑郁症和双相障碍的治疗方法。与其他精神活性药物一样，抗抑郁药物和情绪稳定剂都不能实现“治愈”。然而，它们的使用让许多抑郁症和双相障碍患者的生活有了很大不同。
p27.en: Drug treatment also includes the use of several compounds, which have completely changed the treatment of depression and bipolar disorders. Like other psychoactive drugs, neither antidepressants nor emotional stabilizers can achieve a “cure”. Their use, however, has led to a significant difference in the lives of many persons with depression and dichotomy.

p28.original: 抗抑郁药物 所有三大类抗抑郁药物通过“放大”某些大脑通路传输的信息来发挥作用，尤其是那些使用去甲肾上腺素和血清素的通路（Holmes，2001）。
p28.en: Antidepressants all three main types of antidepressants function by “expanding” information transmitted by certain brain-routing routes, especially those using deadrenalin and serotonin (Homes, 2001).

p29.original: 1. 在神经递质被释放到脑细胞之间的突触后，丙米嗪和阿米替林等三环类化合物减少神经元对神经递质的再吸收——这一过程称为再摄取。
p29.en: After the release of the neurotransmitters to synapses between brain cells, tricyclic compounds such as propamazine and amitilin reduce neuron reabsorption of the neurotransmitters, a process known as re-ingestion.

p30.original: 2. 第二组包括著名的抗抑郁药物百忧解（氟西汀）。这些被称为SSRIs（选择性血清素再摄取抑制剂）的药物会干扰血清素的再摄取。因此，SSRIs可以更长时间地保持血清素的可用性。对许多人来说，这种长期的血清素效应会改善抑郁情绪（Hirschfeld，1999；Kramer，1993）。
p30.en: 2. The second group includes the famous antidepressant Prozac (Fluctine). These drugs, known as SSRis (selective serotonin re-ingestion inhibitors), interfere with serotonin re-ingestion. Therefore, SSRIs can maintain serotonin availability for longer periods. For many, this long-term serotonin effect will improve depression (Hirschfeld, 1999); Kramer, 1993.

p31.original: 3. 第三组抗抑郁药物是单胺氧化酶（MAO）抑制剂，它会限制MAO的活性，MAO是一种分解突触中去甲肾上腺素的化学物质。当MAO被抑制时，更多的去甲肾上腺素可用于通过突触间隙传递神经信息。
p31.en: 3. The third set of antidepressants is a monomamine oxidation (MAO) inhibitor that limits the activity of MAO, which is a chemical substance that decomposes adrenaline in adrenaline. When MAO is suppressed, more adrenaline can be used to transmit neural messages through the synapse gap.

p32.original: 奇怪的是，大多数患者报告，抗抑郁药物开始发挥作用至少需要几周的时间。最近的两项研究表明了可能的原因。
p32.en: Curiously, most patients report that antidepressants take at least a few weeks to start functioning. Two recent studies have shown possible reasons.

p33.original: 在一项实验中，服用常用抗抑郁药物的抑郁症患者在数小时内对积极刺激的反应显著增加，尽管整体抑郁情绪的改善需要更长的时间（Harmer et al.，2009）。根据实验者的说法，这些药物似乎可以扭转患者对情绪事件解释中的“负性偏见”——因此可以通过“更加乐观的镜头”看待世界。然而，情绪的改善不会立即发生，因为患者需要时间来适应更积极的前景（Harmer & Pariante，2012；Makin，2014）。
p33.en: In one experiment, the response to positive irritation by depression patients who use commonly used antidepressants increased significantly within hours, although the improvement of overall depression took longer (Harmer et al., 2009). According to the experimenters, these drugs seem to reverse the “negative bias” in patients' interpretation of emotional events — so the world can be seen in a “more optimistic lens”. However, emotional improvements will not occur immediately, as patients need time to adapt to a more positive outlook (Harmer & Pariente, 2012; Makin, 2014.

p34.original: 第二项研究表明，在动物研究中，抗抑郁药物会刺激大脑海马体中神经元的生长——同样，这也需要时间。没有人能确定为什么海马体似乎与抑郁症有关，但这项工作提供了另一个吸引人的线索：压力会减缓大脑中这一区域新神经元的生长，而这大多时候被认为是一种应激反应（Santarelli et al.，2003）。
p34.en: A second study shows that, in animal studies, antidepressants stimulate neurons in the hull of the brain — similarly, it takes time. No one can determine why the hippos appear to be related to depression, but this work provides another attractive clue: stress slows the growth of new neurons in this part of the brain, which is often considered a stress response (Santarelli et al., 2003).

p35.original: 自杀的可能性在抑郁症的治疗中倍受关注。大多数医疗从业者都认同药物可以降低自杀的可能性（Bower，2007；Harmer & Pariante，2012）。但有研究表明，用于治疗抑郁症的药物可能会激发或放大自杀念头，尤其是在治疗的最初几周，特别是在儿童和青少年群体中（Bower，2004）。一份报告显示，短期服药引发的风险很小——不到1%（Bridge et al.，2007）。显然，目前的情况令人感到困惑，美国食品和药物管理局建议开处方者要谨慎（Bower，2006b；Jick zhjn，2004）。
p35.en: The possibility of suicide is of great concern in the treatment of depression. Most medical practitioners agree that drugs can reduce the likelihood of suicide (Bower, 2007); Harmer & Parante, 2012. However, studies have shown that drugs used to treat depression can stimulate or magnify suicide, especially in the first weeks of treatment, especially among children and young people (Bower, 2004). A report indicates that the risk of short-term medication is low - less than 1 per cent (Bridge et al., 2007). It is clear that the current situation is confusing and that the United States Food and Drug Administration has recommended caution on the part of those who prescribe it (Bower, 2006b); Jick zhjn, 2004.

p36.original: 关于SSRIs的争议 精神病学家和百忧解倡导者彼得·克莱默（Peter Kramer，1993）在他的《聆听百忧解》（Listening to Prozac）一书中，鼓励人们使用这种药物，它不仅可以治疗抑郁症，还可以治疗社交焦虑和害怕被拒绝的感觉。这种说法引起了治疗师的强烈回应，他们担心药物可能会掩盖人们需要面对和解决的心理问题。有些人担心抗抑郁药物的广泛使用可能会导致人口中的大部分人的人格结构发生变化——这些变化可能会带来意想不到的社会后果（Breggin & Breggin，1994；Sleek，1994）。事实上，为抗抑郁药物开出的处方比被诊断患有临床抑郁症的人还多（Coyne，2001）。这个问题似乎在大学校园尤为严重，越来越多的学生正在服用抗抑郁药物（Young，2003）。目前，没有人知道长期改变人类的大脑化学物质可能会带来哪些潜在的危险。
p36.en: The controversy about SSRis, the psychiatrist and Prozac advocate Peter Kramer, in his book " Listening to Prozac ", encourages people to use this drug, which not only treats depression, but also treats social anxiety and fears of rejection. This claim elicited a strong response from the therapists who feared that drugs might mask the psychological problems that people needed to face and address. There are concerns that the widespread use of antidepressants may lead to changes in the personality structure of most of the population — changes that may have unexpected social consequences (Breggin & Breggin, 1994); Sleek, 1994. In fact, antidepressants are more prescribed than those diagnosed with clinical depression (Coyne, 2001). The problem appears to be particularly acute on university campuses, with more and more students taking antidepressants (Young, 2003). At present, no one knows what potential risks could be associated with a long-term change in the brain chemistry of humans.

p37.original: 与医学模型一样令人担忧的是，另一份报告表明，抗抑郁药物的宣传效果可能与其对大脑的治疗效果几乎一样多。根据从美国食品和药物管理局文件中挖掘的数据，显示出积极结果的研究比显示这些药物没有效果的研究被更频繁地发表。虽然这些药物的总体效果优于安慰剂，但对其效果的报告似乎被选择性发表的积极结果夸大了（Turner et al.，2008）。
p37.en: As worrying as the medical model, another report suggests that antidepressants can have almost as much impact as their treatment of the brain. Based on data extracted from FDA documents, studies showing positive results were published more frequently than those showing the ineffectiveness of the drugs. While the overall effects of these drugs are better than those of placebos, reports of their effects appear to have been overstated by selective publication of positive results (Turner et al., 2008).

p38.original: 情绪稳定剂 一种简单的化学物质锂（以碳酸锂的形式存在）已被证明是一种非常有效的治疗双相障碍的情绪稳定剂（Paulus，2007；Schou，1997）。锂不仅是一种抗抑郁药物，它还会影响情绪谱系的两端，抑制情绪波动，否则就会出现无法控制的过度兴奋，以及昏昏欲睡和绝望的抑郁。不幸的是，锂也有一个致命的缺点：当浓度过高时它是有毒的。医生们已经了解到，安全治疗需要在一两周内给予小剂量的锂以增加其在血液中的治疗浓度。然后，作为预防措施，必须对患者的血液定期进行分析，以确保锂的浓度没有上升到危险水平。一项令人欣喜的进展是，科学家们发现了一种有前景的锂替代品来治疗双相障碍（Azar，1994；Walden et al.，1998）。丙戊酸钠（商品名：Depakote），最初被用于治疗癫痫，对大多数双相障碍患者来说似乎比锂更有效果，并且危险的副作用更少（Bowden et al.，2000）。
p38.en: An emotional stabilizer A simple chemical substance of lithium (in the form of lithium carbonate) has proved to be a very effective emotional stabilizer for the treatment of bipolar disorders (Paulus, 2007); Schou, 1997. Lithium is not only an antidepressant drug, but it also affects both ends of the emotional spectrum, inhibits emotional volatility, otherwise there will be uncontrolled over-heating, as well as sleepy and desperate depression. Unfortunately, lithium also has a fatal disadvantage: it is toxic when concentrations are too high. Doctors have learned that safe treatment requires a small dose of lithium within a week or two to increase its therapeutic concentration in blood. Then, as a precautionary measure, the patient's blood must be regularly analysed to ensure that lithium concentrations do not rise to dangerous levels. A welcome development was the discovery by scientists of a promising alternative to lithium to treat the twin-stage barrier (Azar, 1994); Walden et al., 1998). Sodium acetate (trade name: Depakote), initially used for epilepsy treatment, appears to be more effective than lithium for most patients with dichotomy and less dangerous side effects (Bowden et al., 2000).

p40.original: 为了减轻压力和抑制与日常烦恼相关的焦虑，数以百万计的美国人服用抗焦虑药物（antianxiety drug），如巴比妥类药物或苯二氮卓类药物。
p40.en: To relieve stress and to contain anxiety associated with daily distress, millions of Americans take anti-anxiety drugs, such as barbiturates or benzodiazepines.

p41.original: 作为中枢神经系统抑制剂，巴比妥类药物具有放松作用。但是，如果过量服用或服用期间喝酒，可能会很危险。
p41.en: As a central nervous system inhibitor, barbiturates are relaxed. However, it may be dangerous to overdose or to drink alcohol during the time of taking.

p42.original: 相比较而言，苯二氮卓类药物，如安定和阿普唑仑，通过增加神经递质GABA的活性而起作用，从而减少大脑中具体涉及焦虑感的区域的活动。苯二氮卓类药物也被称为“弱镇静剂”。
p42.en: By comparison, benzodiazepine drugs, such as Valium and Apulon, work by increasing the activity of the neurotransmitting GABA, thereby reducing activity in the brain in areas specifically concerned with anxiety. Benzodiazepines are also known as “weak sedatives”.

p43.original: 许多心理学家认为，这些抗焦虑药物（如同抗抑郁药物）被过度使用。本应该由人们面对和解决的问题，不能只用化学物质来掩盖。然而，抗焦虑化合物可用于帮助人们应对特定情况，如手术前的焦虑。以下是关于这些化合物的一些注意事项（Hecht，1986）。
p43.en: Many psychologists believe that these anti-anxiety drugs (like anti-depressants) are overused. The problems that should be faced and solved should not be covered by chemical substances alone. However, anti-anxiety compounds can be used to help people cope with specific situations, such as pre-operative anxiety. The following are some of the concerns regarding these compounds (Hecht, 1986).

p44.original: 如果长期使用巴比妥类药物和苯二氮卓类药物，可能会导致身体和心理成瘾（Holmes，2001；Schatzberg，1991）。
p44.en: The long-term use of barbiturates and benzodiazepines may lead to physical and psychological addiction (Homes, 2001); Schatzberg, 1991.

p45.original: 由于它们对大脑的强大作用，不应将这些药物用于缓解日常生活中常见的压力和焦虑。
p45.en: Because of their powerful effect on the brain, these drugs should not be used to alleviate the stress and anxiety that are common in everyday life.

p46.original: 当面临特定焦虑时，连续服用抗焦虑药物通常不应超过几天。如果服用时间超过此时间，医生应逐渐减少用量。长期使用后突然停药会导致戒断症状，如抽搐、震颤、腹部疼痛和肌肉痉挛。
p46.en: When faced with particular anxiety, continuous anti-anxiety medication should not normally exceed a few days. If the time taken is longer, the doctor should gradually reduce the amount of use. The sudden stoppage of medication after prolonged use leads to absconding symptoms such as convulsions, tremors, abdominal pain and muscle spasms.

p47.original: 由于抗焦虑药物会抑制部分中枢神经系统，因此它们会削弱驾驶、操作机器或执行其他需要警觉性的任务（如学习或考试）的能力。
p47.en: Since anti-anxiety drugs inhibit part of the central nervous system, they weaken the ability to drive, operate machines or perform other tasks requiring vigilance, such as learning or examinations.

p48.original: 与酒精（也是一种中枢神经系统抑制剂）或安眠药一起服用时，抗焦虑药物会导致个体失去知觉甚至死亡。
p48.en: When administered with alcohol (also a central nervous system inhibitor) or sleeping pills, anti-anxiety drugs can lead to loss of consciousness or even death.

p49.original: 最后，一些抗抑郁药物被发现可用于减轻某些焦虑障碍的症状，如惊恐障碍、广场恐怖症、强迫症（现代精神科医生很可能会为弗洛伊德的强迫症患者开抗抑郁药物）。但由于这些问题可能是由于血清素水平下降引起的，因此它们可能对百忧解等专门影响血清素功能的药物反应更好。
p49.en: Finally, some antidepressants have been found to alleviate symptoms of some anxiety disorders, such as panic disorder, plaza terrorism, and coercion (modern psychiatrists are likely to provide antidepressants to Freud's compulsive patients). However, since these problems may be caused by a decline in serotonin levels, they may be more responsive to medicines that specifically affect serotonic functions, such as Prozac.

p51.original: 从咖啡因到尼古丁，从安非他明到可卡因，任何能使人产生兴奋或亢奋的药物都属于兴奋剂（stimulant）。我们已经看到兴奋剂可用于治疗发作性睡病。在治疗注意缺陷/多动障碍（ADHD）方面它们也具有公认的优势。虽然为多动儿童开出兴奋剂（一种常见的药物是哌甲酯）似乎很奇怪，但将兴奋剂疗法与行为疗法和安慰剂进行比较的研究表明，兴奋剂发挥了明显的作用（American Academy of Pediatrics，2001；Meyers，2006）。尽管确切的运行机制尚不清楚，但兴奋剂可能会通过增加大脑中多巴胺、谷氨酸和/或血清素的可用性对多动儿童起作用（Gainetdinov et al.，1999）。
p51.en: From caffeine to nicotine, from amphetamine to cocaine, any drug that can cause excitement or excavation is a stimulant. We've seen stimulants that can be used to treat sexually transmitted sleeping diseases. They also have recognized advantages in treating impairments/mulcanic disorders (ADHD). While it seems strange to prescribe stimulants for children with multiple movements (a common drug is methylether), studies comparing doping therapy with behavioural therapy and placebos show that doping plays a significant role (American Academy of Pediatrics, 2001); Meyers, 2006. Although the exact operating mechanism is not yet clear, stimulants may work for children with multiple movements by increasing the availability of dopamine, azinta and/or serum in the brain (Gainetdinov et al., 1999).

p52.original: 我们可以想象，使用兴奋剂治疗多动儿童已经引起了争议（O'Connor，2001）。当然，一些反对意见源于不了解这些药物会帮助患有此类疾病的儿童安静下来。其他担忧则有更多实质性的内容。对于某些患者，该药物会干扰正常的睡眠模式。此外，有证据表明兴奋剂疗法会减缓儿童的成长和发育（National Institute of Mental Health，2006）。一些合理的担忧还集中在可能造成潜在的药物滥用上，始终存在着这样一种可能，即将每个孩子的行为问题都视为ADHD的症状（Smith，2002a）。最后，批评者指出给儿童开兴奋剂处方可能会鼓励他们以后滥用药物（Daw，2001）。令人高兴的是，最近的研究发现，作为ADHD的治疗方法，认知行为疗法（CBT）的效果可与兴奋剂相当（Sinha，2005）。许多专家认为，更好的方案是采用CBT和兴奋剂的联合治疗。
p52.en: As we can imagine, the use of stimulants for the treatment of children with excessive mobility has been controversial (O'Connell, 2001). Of course, some objections stem from a lack of understanding that these drugs help to calm children with such diseases. Other concerns have more substantive content. For some patients, the drug interferes with normal sleep patterns. In addition, there is evidence that stimulant therapy slows children's growth and development (National Institute of Mental Health, 2006). Some legitimate concerns also focus on the potential for potential drug abuse, and there is always the possibility that the behavioural problems of every child are seen as symptoms of ADHD (Smith, 2002a). Finally, critics have pointed out that prescriptions of doping to children may encourage them to abuse drugs later (Daw, 2001). It is gratifying to note that recent studies have found that cognitive behaviour therapy (CBT) as an ADHD treatment can have comparable effects to stimulants (Sinha, 2005). Many experts considered that a better programme would be to use a combination of CBT and stimulants.

p54.original: 从20世纪50年代开始，药物治疗引发了治疗严重精神障碍的一场革命，当时可用的治疗方法几乎只有谈话疗法、住院治疗、监禁、休克治疗和额叶切除术。当然，迄今为止，没有发现哪种药物能“治愈”任何精神障碍。然而，在许多情况下，这些药物可以通过改变大脑的化学反应来抑制症状。
p54.en: Since the 1950s, drug treatment has led to a revolution in the treatment of severe mental disorders, when almost all available was talk therapy, hospitalization, imprisonment, shock treatment and foetal hysterectomy. To date, of course, no drug has been found to “cure” any mental disorder. In many cases, however, these drugs can inhibit symptoms by changing the chemical reaction of the brain.

p55.original: 但是，所有这些对药物治疗的热情都有保证吗？根据神经科学家埃利奥特·华伦斯坦（Elliot Valenstein，1998）的说法，当我们仔细观察药物治疗的背后时会发现一些重要的问题（Rolnick，1998）。华伦斯坦认为，人们对用药物治疗精神障碍的信心在很大程度上取决于炒作。他将药物治疗被广泛接受归功于制药公司在营销其产品方面进行的巨额投资。尤其令人担忧的是医生为儿童开的也是这些药，尽管许多药物在此类人群中的安全性和有效性尚未被证实（K. Brown，2003a）。
p55.en: But is all this enthusiasm for medication guaranteed? According to the neuroscientist Elliot Valenstein, 1998, when we look closely at the back of the drug treatment, we find some important questions (Ronick, 1998). According to Valentin, confidence in the use of drugs for the treatment of mental disorders depends to a large extent on sex. He attributed the widespread acceptance of drug treatment to the huge investment made by pharmaceutical companies in marketing their products. Of particular concern is the fact that the same medications have been prescribed by doctors for children, although the safety and effectiveness of many of the drugs in this population group have not yet been proven (K. Brown, 2003a).

p56.original: 很少有人质疑药物是治疗某些疾病（如双相障碍和精神分裂症）的最佳治疗方法。然而，在其他许多情况下，药物治疗的明显优势在于见效快且成本低。然而，一些研究对简单用时间和金钱进行衡量的假设提出了质疑。例如，研究表明，从长远来看，单独使用认知行为疗法或与药物相结合来治疗抑郁症、焦虑症和进食障碍比单独使用药物更有效、更经济（Clay，2000；Smith，2012）。然而，有证据表明，近年来心理治疗的使用有所减少，而单纯的药物治疗却有所增加，这可能是因为公众接受了大量的药物广告（Nordal，2010；Olfson & Marcus，2010）。
p56.en: Very few question that drugs are the best treatment for certain diseases, such as bipolar disorders and schizophrenia. In many other cases, however, the obvious advantage of drug treatment is that it is effective and cost-effective. However, a number of studies have questioned the assumption of simple measurement of time and money. For example, studies have shown that, in the long run, the treatment of depression, anxiety and eating disorders is more efficient and economical than the use of drugs alone, either individually or in combination with drugs (Clay, 2000); Smith, 2012. However, there is evidence that the use of psychotherapy has decreased in recent years, while the use of purely pharmaceutical treatment has increased, possibly because of the large number of drug advertisements received by the public (Nordal, 2010); Olfson & Marcus, 2010.

p57.original: 13.8 治疗心理障碍的其他医学疗法
p57.en: 13.8 Other medical treatments for mental disorders

p59.original: 解释如何使用精神外科手术和脑刺激疗法来治疗心理障碍。
p59.en: Explain how psychosurgery and brain irritation therapy are used to treat mental disorders.

p60.original: 《洛杉矶时报》（Los Angeles Times）的一篇文章的标题是“用0.22口径手枪自杀却意外治愈心理障碍”（1988年2月23日）。文章透露，一名患有严重强迫症的19岁男子用手枪从大脑前部射出一颗0.22口径的子弹。令人惊奇的是，他活了下来，其病理症状也消失了，智力没有受到影响。
p60.en: An article in Los Angeles Times entitled “Honnioticly healing psychological disorders with a 0.22 calibre pistol” (23 February 1988). The article revealed that a 19-year-old man suffering from severe coercion had fired a 0.22-caliber bullet from the front of the brain with a pistol. Surprisingly, he survived, his pathological symptoms disappeared and his mental health was not affected.

p61.original: 我们不推荐这种形式的治疗，但该案例确实说明了物理干预对大脑的潜在影响。据此，我们在这里简要介绍两种旨在改变大脑结构和功能的药物治疗的替代疗法。
p61.en: We do not recommend this form of treatment, but the case does illustrate the potential impact of physical intervention on the brain. Accordingly, we would like to briefly describe here two alternative treatments for medication designed to change the structure and functioning of the brain.

p65.original: 长期以来，外科医生一直渴望通过切断大脑各部分之间的联系或切除大脑的一小部分来治疗精神障碍。今天，精神外科手术（psychosurgery）通常被认为是最后的手段。尽管如此，这种做法至少可以追溯到中世纪，当时外科医生可能会打开一个不幸的疯子的头骨，从中取出“愚蠢的石头”（当然，没有这样的“石头”，而且在这些手术中除了酒精之外没有其他麻醉剂）。
p65.en: Surgeons have long been eager to treat mental disorders by cutting links between parts of the brain or removing a small fraction of the brain. Today, psychosurgery (psychosurgery) is usually considered a last resort. Nevertheless, this practice dates back at least to the medieval century, when surgeons could have opened the skull of an unfortunate lunatic and removed from it “soft stones” (and, of course, no such “rocks” and there was no anaesthetic other than alcohol in these operations).

p66.original: 在现代，最著名的精神外科手术是已经被弃用的额叶切除术。这项手术由葡萄牙精神病学家埃加斯·莫尼兹（Egas Moñiz）发明[2]，通过切断连接额叶和大脑结构的某些神经纤维，尤其是丘脑和下丘脑的神经纤维来治疗精神障碍——这很像发生在著名但不幸的菲尼亚斯·盖奇身上的意外，在一次爆炸事故中铁棒穿过了他的额叶，之后他的性格发生了变化。莫尼兹手术的最初选择对象是激越的精神分裂症患者以及强迫症和焦虑症患者。令人惊讶的是，这种很粗暴的手术常常会显著减少激越和焦虑症状。不好的一面则是，手术会永久性地破坏患者性格的基本特点。通常，一些患者在手术后会表现出对个人幸福和周围环境失去兴趣。随着额叶切除术经验的积累，医生发现它破坏了患者提前计划的能力，他们对他人的意见变得毫不在意，他们的行为变得孩子气，他们的智力和情感也变得平淡，自我意识失去了连贯性。毫不奇怪的是，当抗精神病药物在20世纪50年代出现时，并且有望控制精神病症状且没有表现出明显的永久性脑损伤风险时，额叶切除术的时代就结束了（Valenstein，1980）。
p66.en: In modern times, the most famous psychosurgery is the abdominal hysterectomy, which has been abandoned. The operation, invented by the Portuguese psychiatrist Egas Moñiz, treated the mental disorder by cutting off certain neurofibres connected to the forehead and brain structure, especially the neural fibres of the hypothalamus and hypothalamus — much like the accident that occurred in the famous but unfortunate Finyas Gage, whose forehead had been crossed by an iron bar in an explosion, after which his personality changed. The initial selection for the Moniz operation was for people with acute schizophrenia and for people with stress and anxiety. Surprisingly, such harsh operations often reduce stress and anxiety significantly. On the negative side, the operation permanently destroys the basic characteristics of the patient's character. Generally, some patients show a loss of interest in personal well-being and the surrounding environment after the operation. With the accumulation of experience with euphoria, doctors find it to be damaging to patients ' ability to plan ahead, they become insensitive to others, their behaviour becomes childish, their mental and emotional subdued, and their self-aware lacked consistency. It is not surprising that the era of lobotomy is over when antipsychotic drugs appeared in the 1950s, and when it was hoped to control psychiatric symptoms without showing a clear risk of permanent brain damage (Valenstein, 1980).

p67.original: 目前医生偶尔还会进行精神外科手术，但更多的是一些精准的、经过检验的局限于非常特定的脑部障碍的手术。例如，在“裂脑”手术中，切断连接胼胝体（corpus callosum）的纤维可以减少某些癫痫患者危及生命的癫痫发作，而且副作用相对较小。精神外科手术也在大脑中涉及疼痛感知的区域进行，否则会出现顽固性疼痛。然而，今天，DSM-5中的疾病不再采用精神外科手术治疗。
p67.en: Doctors now perform occasional psychiatric surgery, but more often precise, tested and limited to very specific brain disorders. For example, in “breathing” operations, the loss of fibres connected to the corpus callosum can reduce life-threatening epilepsy in some epilepsy patients and have relatively small side effects. Psychosurgery is also carried out in areas of the brain where pain perception is involved, otherwise there is persistent pain. Today, however, DSM-5 diseases are no longer treated for psychosurgery.

p69.original: 脑电刺激，也称电休克疗法（electroconvulsive therapy，ECT），目前仍被广泛使用，特别是针对对药物或心理治疗没有反应的严重抑郁症患者（你应该还记得治疗师说德里克不适合采用ECT）。治疗通过向患者的太阳穴短暂——从0.1秒到1秒——施加电流（75伏到100伏），从而引起抽搐。抽搐通常会在不到1分钟的时间内结束。医生通过使用短效巴比妥类药物和肌肉松弛剂让患者“入睡”，以为这种创伤性干预做好准备。这不仅会使患者失去知觉，而且在癫痫发作期间最大限度地减少任何剧烈的身体痉挛（Abrams，1992；Malitz & Sackheim，1984）。半小时后患者苏醒，但他们对癫痫发作或治疗准备工件没有任何记忆。
p69.en: EMPs, also known as electroshock therapy (electroconvulsive technique, ECT), are still widely used, especially for severely depressed patients who do not respond to medication or psychotherapy (you should recall that the therapist said that Derek was not fit to use ECT). The treatment causes convulsions through electric currents (75 to 100 volts) that are applied to patients' temples for short periods — from 0.1 to 1 second. The convulsions usually end in less than one minute. Doctors prepare patients for this traumatic intervention by “sleeping” with short-act barbiturants and muscle relaxants. This not only results in the patient being unconscious, but also minimizes any severe physical convulsions during epilepsy (Abrams, 1992); Malitz & Sackheim, 1984. After half an hour, the patients woke up, but they had no memory of the epilepsy or the preparation of the treatment.

p70.original: 电休克疗法有效吗？这种治疗通过向一个人的头骨和大脑发送电流，尽管看起来很粗暴，但研究表明，ECT是治疗抑郁症的有效工具，尤其是对那些有自杀倾向的人，他们需要一种比药物或心理治疗更快的干预措施（Lilienfeld & Arkowitz，2014；Shorter & Healy，2007）。通常，与药物治疗所需的1到2周相比，采用ECT的抑郁症患者的症状会在3或4天的治疗中有所减轻。
p70.en: Does electroshock therapy work? This treatment is transmitted to a person's skull and brain, although it appears to be brutal, but studies show that ECT is an effective tool for treating depression, especially for those with suicidal tendencies, who need a faster intervention than medication or psychotherapy (Lilienfeld & Arkowitz, 2014); Shorter & Healy 2007. Typically, the symptoms of ECT-using depression are reduced in 3 or 4 days of treatment compared to the 1 to 2 weeks required for drug treatment.

p71.original: 虽然大多数临床医生认为，只要操作得当，ECT是安全且有效的，但一些批评者担心它也可能被滥用以压制反对的声音或惩罚不合作的患者（Butcher et al.，2008；Holmes，2001）。对ECT的其他担忧源于其影响尚不明确。迄今为止，还没有明确的理论解释为什么诱导轻度惊厥可以缓解紊乱的症状，尽管有一些迹象表明它可能会刺激大脑部分神经元的生长，特别是海马体。
p71.en: While most clinicians believe that ECT is safe and effective as long as it works properly, some critics fear that it may also be misused to silence opposition voices or punish non-cooperative patients (Butcher et al., 2008); Holmes, 2001. Other concerns about ECT stem from the uncertainty about its impact. To date, there is no clear theory why the induction of mild convulsions can mitigate the symptoms of disorders, although there are some indications that it may stimulate the growth of some neurons in the brain, especially the hippos.

p72.original: 最令人担忧的情况也许是电休克疗法可能会引起记忆缺陷（Breggin，1979，1991）。然而，支持者声称，患者通常会在治疗后数月内恢复全部记忆（Calev et al.，1991）。面对这样的担忧，美国国家心理健康研究所调查了ECT的使用情况，并于1985年谨慎地支持它用于治疗小范围的障碍，尤其是重度抑郁症。然后，在1990年，美国精神病学会也宣布ECT是一种有效的治疗选项。然而，为了尽量减少即使是短期的副作用，ECT通常是“单侧”进行的——仅在右侧太阳穴进行——以减少导致语言功能受损的可能性。
p72.en: Perhaps the most worrying situation is that electroconvulsive therapy may cause memory defects (Breggin, 1979, 1991). However, supporters claim that patients usually recover their full memory within months of treatment (Calev et al., 1991). Faced with this concern, the National Institute of Mental Health of the United States investigated the use of ECT and carefully supported its use in 1985 to treat small-scale barriers, particularly severe depression. Then, in 1990, the American Psychiatric Institute also declared ECT to be an effective treatment option. However, in order to minimize even short-term side effects, ECTs are usually “one-sided” — only on the right — to reduce the likelihood of damage to the language function.

p73.original: 作为一种有前途的新治疗工具，用磁场刺激大脑可以带来像ECT一样的好处且不存在导致记忆丧失的风险。经颅磁刺激（transcranial magnetic stimulation，TMS）仍处于实验阶段，它主要涉及将高功率磁刺激定向到大脑的特定部位。研究表明，TMS不仅可用于治疗抑郁症，还可用于治疗精神分裂症和双相障碍（George，2003；Weir，2013）。由于TMS疗法与电休克疗法不同，不需要镇静，也不会引起癫痫发作，因此研究人员希望它能够成为一种替代ECT的更安全的治疗方案。
p73.en: As a promising new treatment tool, magnetic field stimulation of the brain can offer the same benefits as ECT and there is no risk of loss of memory. Transcription magnetic stimulator (TMS) is still in the experimental phase, which mainly involves directing high-power magnetic irritation to specific parts of the brain. Studies have shown that TMS can be used not only to treat depression but also schizophrenia and dichotomy (George, 2003); Weir, 2013. Since the TMS therapy, unlike electroconvulsive therapy, does not need to be sedated and does not cause epilepsy, researchers expect it to be a safer treatment alternative to ECT.

p74.original: TMS的效果如何？在迄今为止的研究中，TMS使大约35%到40%的重度抑郁症患者的症状有所改善，并能保持数月（George et al.，2013）。这个结果有多好？这相当于或超过了服用抗抑郁药物得以改善的患者数量。研究人员希望TMS与认知行为疗法相结合会更加有效。
p74.en: How's TMS working? In studies to date, TMS has improved the symptoms of approximately 35 to 40 per cent of the severely depressed population and has been able to sustain them for months (George et al., 2013). How good is this? This corresponds to or exceeds the number of patients who have improved their access to antidepressants. Researchers hope that the combination of TMS and cognitive behaviour therapy will be more effective.

p75.original: 最近，神经病学家海伦·梅伯格（Helen Mayberg）报告了使用深度脑刺激的方法，这需要用外科手术通过颅骨上的一个小孔将微电极直接植入大脑，在那里它向额叶的特定区域提供持续的电流。梅伯格博士将这种治疗比作“起搏器”，用于治疗抑郁症患者似乎无法控制的皮质区域（Gutman，2006；Price，2009）。尽管该治疗仅用于少数患者，但梅伯格报告的结果令人非常振奋（Mayberg et al.，2005）。她认为TMS不仅仅是其他疗法的一种替代方法，更是那些对其他疗法没有反应的重度抑郁症患者的希望。
p75.en: Recently, neurologist Helen Mayberg has reported on the use of deep brain irritation, which requires the microelectric pole to be directly implanted into the brain through a small hole in the skull, where it provides continuous currents to specific areas of the forehead. Dr. Meborg compared this treatment to a “pacifier” used to treat the seemingly uncontrollable cortical areas of depression (Gutman, 2006); Price, 2009. Although the treatment was used only for a small number of patients, the results reported by Meberg were very encouraging (Mayberg et al., 2005). In her view, the TMS was not just an alternative to other treatments, but also a hope for those with severe depression who did not respond to other treatments.

p76.original: 13.9 住院治疗和其他替代方案

p78.original: 描述美国精神病院的历史。
p78.en: The history of American psychiatric hospitals.

p79.original: 我们已经看到，精神病院最初被设想为避难所——“庇护所”。在那里，精神失常的人们可以逃避日常生活给他们带来的压力。事实上，开始时精神病院很好地发挥了作用（Maher & Maher，1985）。但到了20世纪，这些医院已经变得人满为患，从某种意义上成了无家可归的精神病患者的仓库。有钱人很少去这些机构治疗，取而代之的是，他们有私人护理，包括个体心理治疗（Doyle，2002a）。
p79.en: As we have seen, the psychiatric hospital was originally conceived as a shelter — a “shelter”. There, people with mental disorders can escape the stress they face in their daily lives. In fact, the psychiatric hospital had worked well at first (Maher & Maher, 1985). By the twentieth century, however, these hospitals had become overcrowded and, in a sense, had become warehouses for homeless mentally ill people. The rich rarely go to these institutions for treatment, replacing them with private care, including individual psychotherapy (Doyle, 2002a).

p80.original: 一直到20世纪50年代，药物对精神病院中的治疗方法产生了一些深刻的改变。在此之前，住院病人经常发现自己要穿上束身衣、待在上锁的房间里，有时还要接受额叶切除术。同时，在大型公立精神病院，心理治疗是一种微弱的“团体治疗”形式，一次对整个病房的患者——可能是50人——进行治疗。太多的病人、太少的治疗师、太少的时间，使得这样的治疗几乎毫无用处。
p80.en: Until the 1950s, drugs had brought about some profound changes in treatment in psychiatric institutions. Prior to this, inpatients often found themselves in straitjacket, locked rooms and sometimes subject to frontal ectomy. At the same time, in large public psychiatric hospitals, psychotherapy is a weak form of “group therapy” that treats patients — possibly 50 people — throughout the ward at once. Too many patients, too few therapists, too little time, make such treatment almost useless.

p81.original: 13.9.1 去机构化和社区精神卫生服务
p81.en: 13.9.1 Deinstitutionalization and Community Mental Health Services

p82.original: 抗精神病药物的问世带来了巨大的变化。成千上万服用新药物有效果的患者被送回家，然后接受门诊治疗。去机构化（deinstitutionalization）的目标就是让尽可能多的患者返回他们生活的社区，在那里他们（希望）在熟悉和支持的环境中健康生活。这个概念也受到政治家们的欢迎，因为他们不想看到大量资金被投入精神病院（顺便说一句，里面都是无投票权的患者）。因此，到20世纪70年代，政治家和精神卫生专业人员达成了共识，即主要治疗场所应从精神病院转移到社区。在那里，诊所可以提供心理和药物治疗，康复患者可以与家人、寄养家庭或组合家庭住在一起。这一愿景被称为社区精神卫生运动（commmunity mental health movement）。
p82.en: The advent of anti-psychiatric drugs has brought about tremendous change. Tens of thousands of patients who had the effect of taking new drugs were sent home for outpatient treatment. The goal of deinstitutionalization is to return as many patients as possible to the communities in which they live, where they (hope) live healthyly in a familiar and supportive environment. This concept has also been welcomed by politicians who do not want to see large sums of money invested in psychiatric institutions (by the way, all of them are non-voting patients). Thus, by the 1970s, there was consensus among politicians and mental health professionals that the main treatment places should be transferred from psychiatric institutions to the community. There, the clinic can provide psychological and pharmaceutical treatment, and rehabilitation patients can live with their families, foster families or group families. This vision is known as community mental health movement.

p83.original: 不幸的是，现实与愿景并不相符（Doyle，2002a；Torrey，1996，1997）。社区精神卫生诊所——社区精神卫生运动的核心——很少得到它们需要的全部资金。慢性病患者从精神病院出院后，他们回到的是那些提供很少治疗资源的社区和无力照顾他们的家庭（Smith et al.，1993）。最终，需要照顾的精神病患者挤满了当地综合医院的精神科病房——而不是精神病院。结果是，在美国，住院治疗继续占据了很大一部分精神卫生的支出（Kiesler，1993；U.S.Department of Health and Human Services，2002）。
p83.en: Unfortunately, reality does not match vision (Doyle, 2002a); Torrey, 1996 (1997). Community mental health clinics — the core of the community mental health movement — rarely receive the full funding they need. When people with chronic illnesses are discharged from psychiatric hospitals, they return to communities that provide little resources for treatment and families that are unable to take care of them (Smith et al., 1993). Ultimately, the psychiatric patients in need of care are packed with psychiatric wards in local general hospitals — not psychiatric hospitals. As a result, hospitalization continues to account for a significant proportion of mental health spending in the United States (Kisler, 1993); U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, 2002).

p84.original: 去机构化使精神病患者重新回到社区，但社区往往没有足够的资源继续为他们提供治疗。许多人最终流落街头，无家可归。
p84.en: Deinstitutionalization brings the mentally ill back into the community, which often does not have sufficient resources to continue to treat them. Many end up living on the streets, homeless.

p85.original: 尽管我们描绘了黑暗的一面，但社区治疗还是取得了一些成功。凯斯勒（Kiesler，1982）回顾了10项研究并报告说，其中精神病患者被随机分配到医院治疗或各种社区治疗计划中，当患者能够得到这些服务时，他们的情况在基于社区的项目中更常能得到改善。此外，接受社区治疗的人以后住院的可能性较小。当这些项目拥有足够的资源时，它们会非常有效（McGuire，2000）。
p85.en: Despite the dark side that we have painted, community treatment has had some success. Kiesler, 1982 reviewed 10 studies and reported that mental patients were assigned to hospitals at random or to various community treatment schemes, and that their situation was more often improved in community-based projects when patients had access to these services. In addition, persons receiving community treatment are less likely to be hospitalized later. These projects will be very effective when they have sufficient resources (McGuire, 2000).

p86.original: 13.9.2 满足未被满足的精神卫生服务需求
p86.en: 13.9.2 Meeting Unmet Mental Health Services Needs

p87.original: 如你所见，我们已经有一套被证明有效的治疗方法。但另一方面，需要治疗的人比实际得到治疗的人要多得多（Clay，2012）。一部分问题是缺乏服务提供者，包括心理学家、精神病学家、社会工作者和精神科护士。另一部分问题是大约6000万美国人生活在农村地区，无法便捷地获得精神卫生服务。当然，多亏了互联网和电话，他们中的一些人现在可以通过“远程医疗”咨询获得帮助（Novotney，2011；Stambor，2006；Winerman，2006c）。通过远程医疗方法，心理学家和其他专业人士可以快速地与偏远地区的来访者建立联系，以回答疑问、进行转诊，甚至提供治疗。
p87.en: As you can see, we already have a proven cure. On the other hand, there are far more people in need of treatment than actually received (Clay, 2012). Part of the problem is the lack of service providers, including psychologists, psychiatrists, social workers and psychiatric nurses. Another part of the problem is that some 60 million Americans live in rural areas and lack easy access to mental health services. Of course, thanks to the Internet and telephone, some of them now have access to “telemedicine” counselling (Novotney, 2011); Stambor, 2006; Winerman, 2006c. Through telemedicine methods, psychologists and other professionals can quickly contact visitors in remote areas to answer questions, make referrals and even provide treatment.

p88.original: 考虑到这些计划仍然只惠及少数需要帮助的人，心理学家阿兰·凯兹丁（Alan Kazdin）和斯泰西·伯莱斯（Stacey Blasé，2011）呼吁彻底“重启”心理治疗。他们告诫我们要认识到，目前的治疗方法强调一对一的咨询和心理治疗——然而，尽管这种治疗有效，但永远无法满足全部需要。凯兹丁和伯莱斯说，我们需要的主要是新的服务系统和资金，能够支持更多人参与的计划。这些不仅包括远程医疗计划的扩展，还包括旨在预防、克服治疗中的种族、民族和语言障碍以及清除日常障碍的举措，如缺乏交通工具、带孩子的保姆和适当的保险。今天，这就是心理治疗的最新进展。
p88.en: Considering that these programmes continue to benefit only a small number of people in need, psychologists Alan Kazdin and Stacey Blasé, 2011 call for a complete “re-start” of psychotherapy. They cautioned us to recognize that the current treatment emphasizes one-on-one counselling and psychological treatment — yet, despite its effectiveness, it will never be able to meet all needs. Cezdin and Preston said that what we need is mainly new service systems and funding that can support plans for more people to participate. These include not only the expansion of telemedicine programmes, but also initiatives aimed at prevention, overcoming racial, ethnic and linguistic barriers to treatment and removing daily barriers, such as lack of transportation, child-sitters and appropriate insurance. Today, this is the latest development in psychological care.

p89.original: “远程医疗”为农村地区的患者提供了精神卫生服务，否则这些地区的人可能无法获得帮助。
p89.en: Telemedicine provides mental health services to patients in rural areas, where otherwise people may not be able to access help.

p90.original: 心理学很有用 你推荐哪种疗法
p90.en: Psychology works. What kind of therapy do you recommend?

p91.original: 既然我们已经学习了心理疗法和生物医学疗法，请你考虑以下情况。一位朋友把他或她遇到的一些个人问题告诉你，并请你帮助寻找治疗师。由于你正在学习心理学，因此你的朋友会认为，你可能知道什么疗法是最好的。
p91.en: Since we have studied psychotherapy and biomedical therapy, please consider the following. A friend told you about some personal problems he or she had encountered and asked you to help find a therapist. Because you're learning psychology, your friends will think you might know what's best for therapy.

p93.original: 首先，你可以倾听、接纳和探索其他替代方案等。事实上，这可能就是你陷入困境的朋友所需要的。但是，如果你的朋友想寻求治疗师的帮助，或者他或她的情况看起来需要专业帮助，你可以利用你所拥有的精神障碍和治疗方面的知识来帮助你的朋友决定哪类治疗师可能是最合适的。你们应该知道，如果你的朋友所需的治疗超出了治疗师的专业领域，任何有能力的治疗师都会将来访者转诊到别处。
p93.en: First of all, you can listen, accept and explore alternatives, etc. In fact, this may be what your troubled friends need. But if your friend wants help from a therapist, or if his or her situation appears to require professional help, you can use your knowledge of mental disorders and treatment to help your friend decide which kind of therapist may be the most appropriate. As you know, if the treatment that your friend needs goes beyond the therapist's area of specialization, any able therapist will refer the visitor elsewhere.

p95.original: 那么，在推荐特定类型的治疗师之前，你需要考虑以下一些问题。
p95.en: So, before you can recommend a particular type of therapist, you need to consider the following questions.

p96.original: 是否需要医学治疗？虽然你不应该试图做出诊断，但如果你怀疑朋友的问题涉及严重的精神障碍，如精神病、躁狂症或双相障碍，你应该鼓励你的朋友去找医学专家，如精神科医生或执业护士。如果你怀疑他或她患有嗜睡症、睡眠呼吸暂停、癫痫、阿尔茨海默病或其他被认为具有生物学基础的问题，也需要进行医学评估。如果你的怀疑得到证实，治疗可能包括药物治疗和心理治疗相结合。
p96.en: Do you need medical treatment? Although you should not attempt to make a diagnosis, if you suspect that the problems of a friend involve serious mental disorders, such as mental illness, mania or bipolar disorders, you should encourage your friend to seek medical specialists, such as psychiatrists or practising nurses. A medical assessment is also required if you suspect that he or she suffers from sleeping disorders, sleep breathing pauses, epilepsy, Alzheimer's disease or other issues deemed to have a biological basis. If your suspicions are confirmed, treatment may include a combination of medication and psychological treatment.

p97.original: 是否存在特定行为问题？例如，你的朋友是想消除对蜘蛛的恐惧还是对飞行的恐惧？孩子叛逆？性问题？是否抑郁——但不是精神病？如果是这样，心理咨询或临床心理学家的行为疗法或认知行为疗法可能是最好的选择（精神科医生和其他医学从业者通常没有接受过这类培训）。你可以致电治疗师，询问有关其培训经历和专业领域的信息。
p97.en: Is there a problem of specific conduct? For example, is your friend trying to eliminate the fear of spiders or the fear of flight? The child rebelled? Sex? Is it depression -- not mental? If this is the case, either psycho-counselling or behavioural or cognitive therapy for clinical psychologists may be the best option (psychiatricians and other medical practitioners usually do not receive such training). You can call the therapist and ask him for information about their training experience and their fields of specialization.

p98.original: 团体治疗会有帮助吗？许多人在团体环境中会找到有价值的帮助和支持，在那里他们不仅可以向治疗师学习，还可以向其他团体成员学习。团体治疗在处理害羞、没有自信、成瘾以及复杂的人际关系问题方面特别有效（团体治疗通常比个人治疗便宜）。受过多个学科培训（包括心理学、精神病学和社会工作）的专业人员，都可以带领治疗团队。同样，最好的选择是寻找接受过团体治疗培训的治疗师，并且从以前的来访者那里听到了关于他的好评。
p98.en: Will group therapy help? Many find valuable help and support in group settings, where they can learn not only from therapists but also from other group members. Group therapy is particularly effective in dealing with shyness, lack of self-confidence, addiction and complex interpersonal problems (group therapy is usually cheaper than individual treatment). Professionals trained in various disciplines (including psychology, psychiatry and social work) can lead treatment teams. Similarly, the best option would be to find a therapist who had been trained in group therapy and to hear from former visitors about him.

p99.original: 问题是压力、困惑还是选择？大多数陷入困境的人都不会完全归入我们在上面讨论的类别之一。更典型的是，他们需要有人帮助整理生活中的混乱，找到一种模式制订应对计划。这是领悟疗法的领域。
p99.en: The question is stress, confusion or choice? The majority of those in distress will not be in one of the categories that we discussed above. More typically, they need someone to help sort out the chaos in their lives and find a model for a response plan. This is the area of epithetic therapy.

p101.original: 现在我们对人类生物学、行为和心理过程有了足够的了解，需要规避某些治疗。以下是一些特别重要的例子。
p101.en: We now have enough knowledge of human biology, behaviour and psychological processes to circumvent certain treatments. The following are some particularly important examples.

p102.original: 要避免的药物治疗。轻微的镇静剂（抗焦虑药物）会被过于频繁地用于长期压力大的患者。正如我们所说，由于这些药物的成瘾和镇静作用，它们只能短期服用——如果需要的话。同样，一些医生忽视了催眠药物对失眠患者的危害。虽然这些药物是合法的，但许多此类处方可能会导致药物依赖，并且干扰患者去改变导致问题的根源。
p102.en: To avoid drug treatment. Minor sedatives (anti-anxiety drugs) are used too frequently for chronically stressful patients. As we have said, because of their addiction and sedated effects, these drugs can be taken only for short periods — if needed. Similarly, some doctors have ignored the dangers of hypnotic drugs for insomnia patients. While these drugs are legal, many of these prescriptions can lead to drug dependence and interfere with patients to change the root causes of the problem.

p103.original: 要避免的建议和解释。虽然心理动力学疗法可能会有所帮助，但你也应提醒患者，一些治疗师可能会在愤怒管理问题上提供不明智的建议。从传统角度出发，弗洛伊德学派认为，容易发怒或有暴力倾向的人内心深处有着需要发泄的攻击性。但是，正如我们所看到的，研究表明，试图通过攻击性行为（如大喊或敲打枕头）来发泄自己的攻击性，实际上可能会导致攻击行为增加。
p103.en: Recommendations and explanations to be avoided. While psychodynamic therapy may help, you should also remind patients that some therapists may be unwise to advise on anger management. From a traditional perspective, Freudists believe that people who are prone to anger or violent tendencies have an aggressive nature that needs to be ventilated. However, as we have seen, research shows that attempts to excite themselves through offensive behaviour (such as shouting or knocking on pillows) may actually lead to an increase in attacks.

p104.original: 记住这些注意事项，然后，你的朋友可以同时联系几位治疗师，看看哪位治疗师的技能和方式最适合其问题和个性。
p104.en: Remembering these concerns, then your friends can contact several therapists at the same time to see which therapist's skills and approaches are best suited to their problems and personality.
